Its azimuth of 86° places it almost due east, slightly north of due east.

The main practical caveat is obstruction: in Anchorage, terrain, buildings, trees, and local haze near the horizon could hide it at only 11° altitude. But if you have a reasonably open view toward the east, it should stand out clearly. Its ~101° separation from the Sun means it is nowhere near twilight glare; with the Sun 50° below the horizon, the sky is fully dark.

So: clear sky plus an open eastern horizon = you should be able to spot it without optical aid.
